# onetsolutions_hosting_wordpress (Resource)

Manages a WordPress site installed on an OnetSolutions web hosting.

The web hosting must be active, and the domain must run a PHP version WordPress supports: set it
with `onetsolutions_hosting_php_version` first, as in the example below.

!> **Destroying deletes the site with its content.** A destroy, or a change of `hosting_id`,
`domain` or `path` (which replaces the site), deletes the WordPress site with its files and its
database; `terraform plan` warns about it. Back the site up first if you need its content.
`deletion_protection = true` refuses the destroy.

## Installation inputs

`admin_user`, `admin_password`, `admin_email`, `title` and `language` are applied when the site
is installed only: they are required to install it, and a later change is stored in the state with
a plan-time warning and changes nothing in WordPress; change them in WordPress itself. After an
import they are taken from the configuration without a warning. `admin_password` is kept in the
Terraform state, marked sensitive: protect the state.

## Updates

A site is installed on the latest WordPress version. Change `update_trigger` to any new value to
update it to the latest version, in place; `version` then reads the version installed.

An existing site is imported by its identifier, `<hosting_id>/<id>`: the
`onetsolutions_hosting_wordpress_sites` data source lists the `id` of each site of a web hosting.

Sign-in links to the site's administration are short-lived credentials: the provider does not
read them, use the console.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "wordpress_admin_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

# WordPress needs a recent PHP version on its domain: set it first.
resource "onetsolutions_hosting_php_version" "site" {
  hosting_id  = onetsolutions_web_hosting.site.id
  php_version = "ea-php83"
}

resource "onetsolutions_hosting_wordpress" "site" {
  hosting_id = onetsolutions_hosting_php_version.site.hosting_id
  domain     = onetsolutions_hosting_php_version.site.domain
  path       = "blog"
  title      = "Our blog"
  language   = "fr"

  # Applied at installation only.
  admin_user     = "editor"
  admin_password = var.wordpress_admin_password
  admin_email    = "webmaster@example.fr"

  # Change the value to update WordPress to its latest version.
  update_trigger = "2026-11"

  deletion_protection = true
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `domain` (String) The domain of the web hosting the site is installed on: its primary domain, a subdomain or an addon domain. Changing it replaces the site.
- `hosting_id` (String) The UUID of the web hosting. Changing it replaces the site.

### Optional

- `admin_email` (String) The e-mail address of the site's administrator, required to install the site. Applied at installation only.
- `admin_password` (String, Sensitive) The password of the site's administrator, required to install the site. It is kept in the Terraform state, so protect the state. Applied at installation only: changing it does not change the password. At least 8 characters, with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a digit and a special character.
- `admin_user` (String) The login of the site's administrator, required to install the site. Applied at installation only.
- `deletion_protection` (Boolean) Whether destroying (or replacing) the site is refused. Defaults to `false`. Set it to `false` and apply before destroying a protected site.
- `language` (String) The site's language code, such as `fr` or `en`. When unset, `en`. Applied at installation only.
- `organization_id` (String) The organization the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `organization_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `path` (String) The directory under the domain the site is installed in, such as `blog`, without leading or trailing slash. Defaults to `""`, the root of the domain. Changing it replaces the site.
- `project_id` (String) The project the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `title` (String) The site's title. When unset, `WordPress`. Applied at installation only.
- `update_trigger` (String) Any value: changing it updates the site to the latest WordPress version, in place. Not used when the site is installed, which installs the latest version.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The identifier of the WordPress site on its web hosting, such as `26_40001`, as `onetsolutions_hosting_wordpress_sites` lists it; it is the last part of the import ID.
- `version` (String) The installed WordPress version.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = onetsolutions_hosting_wordpress.site
  id = "3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/4c3b2a1f-0e9d-4c8b-9a7f-6e5d4c3b2a1f/26_40001"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <organization_id>/<project_id>/<hosting_id>/<id>, or <hosting_id>/<id> when the provider sets organization_id and project_id.
# The installation inputs (admin_user, admin_password, admin_email, title, language) are taken
# from the configuration after an import, without a warning.
terraform import onetsolutions_hosting_wordpress.site 3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/4c3b2a1f-0e9d-4c8b-9a7f-6e5d4c3b2a1f/26_40001
```
